title: PetroPoin points liability — restatement for the CFO
prompt:
You are Citra Widyastuti, Analyst at Aurelian & Co., on the PetroNusa engagement (loyalty workstream). It is early August 2025. The PetroPoin current-state assessment was accepted at SteerCo 4 in June; the workstream's working summary and the manager's handoff note are in the project folder, alongside the client's own programme documentation.

Marcus Whelan forwards this from the CFO:

---
Subject: PetroPoin — points liability, before the auditors get to it

Marcus,

Our external auditors have started asking about the loyalty programme balance and I do not have an answer I would sign. What I need from your team is a defensible statement of the PetroPoin points position at FY2024 year-end:

- the gross outstanding balance, and the amount we should actually be carrying as an expected obligation;
- how the balance moved across FY2024 on the programme's own trading during the year, expressed against the opening balance;
- what a point is worth to a member when they use it, and what we expect it to cost us;
- what the carried obligation amounts to per enrolled member.

Every figure with its basis stated on the face of the workbook. Where the folder contains more than one figure for the same thing, tell me which one you have used and why the others are not it. Do not go near the wallet sourcing question — that is settled.

Hendra
---

Work in SRP unless a figure is more naturally stated otherwise, and make the arithmetic traceable cell by cell.

Deliverables: a liability workbook in Excel and a short memo for Hendra. Save them as `petropoin_points_liability_model.xlsx` and `petropoin_points_liability_memo.docx` in your output directory.

checks.description: FY2024 growth in the outstanding points balance generated by the year's own issuance, redemptions and expiry, over the opening balance: (18.7 - 14.2 - 0.5)/78.2*100 = 5.115%. The reported closing balance includes a 5.2 bn prior-period accrual catch-up.

refs.name: adj_note
refs.quote: Includes a prior-period accrual catch-up of 5.2 SRP bn following the Q4 points-engine reconciliation

checks.report_ask: Report the FY2024 growth in the outstanding points balance produced by that year's own points activity, as a percentage of the opening balance.

decoy.description: Taking the reported closing balance against the opening balance, i.e. leaving the prior-period accrual catch-up inside the year's movement.

checks.description: Net expected obligation at FY2024 year-end = gross closing balance 87.4 SRP bn x (1 - approved actuarial breakage of 38.2%) = 54.0132 SRP bn.

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the net outstanding points obligation PetroNusa should be carrying at FY2024 year-end, in SRP bn.

decoy.description: Applying the breakage rate published in the client-facing programme documentation (~45%) to the gross balance.

checks.description: Value a member realises per point = 5 litres of fuel at the current pump price per 500 points = 5 x 13,500 / 500 = 135 SRP per point.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

checks.report_ask: Report the value a member realises per PetroPoin point when they redeem, in SRP per point.

decoy.description: Dividing the pump price by the 500-point redemption threshold, ignoring that the redemption delivers five litres.

checks.description: Expected cost per point issued = 135 SRP redemption value x (1 - 38.2% approved breakage) = 83.43 SRP.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the cost PetroNusa expects to bear per PetroPoin point issued, in SRP per point.

decoy.description: Using the superseded ~45% breakage figure carried in the client-facing programme documentation.

checks.description: Net obligation per enrolled member = 87.4bn x (1-0.382) x 1e9 / 4,219,000 enrolled members on the v2 CRM extract = 12,802.4 SRP.

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the net outstanding points obligation per enrolled member, in SRP per member.

decoy.description: Dividing the gross balance by the registered-member figure published in the client-facing programme documentation.

checks.description: deliverable exists
deliverable exists

difficulty_rationale: Two live traps. (1) The FY2024 ledger row does not foot: the reported closing balance of 87.4 SRP bn includes a 5.2 bn prior-period accrual catch-up carried in the far-right adjustments column, so the year's own trading adds only 4.0 bn, not 9.2 bn. (2) The client-facing Programme Overview publishes a ~45% breakage rate, which the handoff note records as a superseded 2021 estimate on a 24-month window; the approved rate is the 38.2% actuarial estimate settled at the May 2025 review. Per-point value requires combining the 500-points-for-5-litres redemption rule with the pump price (naive path divides pump price by 500), and the per-member figure requires the v2 CRM enrolled base of 4,219,000 rather than the Programme Overview's 2,100,000.

title: PetroPoin earn rate — per-litre margin headroom test
prompt:
You are Citra Widyastuti, Analyst at Aurelian & Co., PetroNusa engagement (loyalty workstream). It is early August 2025. The loyalty current-state assessment was accepted at SteerCo 4 in June; the working summary, the handoff note and the client's programme documentation are all in the project folder, along with the CRM and transaction extracts.

Marcus Whelan writes:

---
Subject: Earn rate — the per-litre arithmetic, before SteerCo 5

Citra,

Mei-Ling's line to the steering group was that customers love points, so double the earn rate. Bambang is half-persuaded. Before we argue about tiers and cashback I want the narrow question answered properly: what does the earn actually cost us on the litre that earns it, and is there room under the fuel margin to double it.

So, per litre of fuel, on the current indicative pump price and fuel gross margin in the research file:

1. what the programme is issuing today per litre;
2. what that costs us, on an expected basis, per litre;
3. that cost against the fuel gross margin on the same litre;
4. what is left of the fuel gross margin per litre if the earn is doubled as proposed;
5. the most we could issue per litre and still respect Bambang's constraint, which is that reward cost on the earning litre must not exceed one fifth of the fuel gross margin on that litre.

Do not rely on any single document's description of the mechanic — reconcile what the programme says it does with what its records show it doing, and be explicit in the memo about which reading each number sits on. Wallet sourcing stays with Hendra's team; stay in our lane.

Thanks, Marcus
---

Deliverables: a headroom model in Excel with the per-litre build visible, and a short memo. Save them as `petropoin_earn_rate_headroom_model.xlsx` and `petropoin_earn_rate_headroom_memo.docx` in your output directory.

checks.description: Points per litre evidenced in the FY2024 transaction extract: 122 points on 12.2 litres = 10 points per litre, consistent across all fuel rows carrying points.

refs.name: ratio_note
refs.quote: the points column is exactly ten times the litres column

checks.report_ask: Report the number of points the programme is currently issuing per litre of fuel.

decoy.description: Taking the earn rate as documented in the client-facing programme overview.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Expected reward cost per earning litre = 10 points x (5 x 13,500 / 500) x (1 - 0.382) = 834.3 SRP per litre.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the reward cost PetroNusa expects to bear per litre of fuel earned on, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Costing the documented one-point-per-litre rule instead of the rate the records show.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Expected reward cost per earning litre (834.3 SRP) as a percentage of fuel gross margin per litre (513 SRP) = 162.63%.

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the reward cost per earning litre as a percentage of the fuel gross margin on that same litre.

decoy.description: Costing points at full face redemption value with no breakage allowance.

checks.description: Fuel gross margin per litre left after reward cost if the earn rate is doubled = 513 - 2 x 834.3 = -1,155.6 SRP per litre.

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the fuel gross margin remaining per litre after reward cost if the earn rate is doubled as proposed, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Doubling the documented one-point-per-litre rule rather than the earn the records show.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Maximum points per litre within a cap of one fifth of fuel gross margin = 0.2 x 513 / (135 x 0.618) = 1.2298 points per litre.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

refs.name: breakage_note
refs.quote: estimate of 38.2% of gross outstanding

checks.report_ask: Report the maximum number of points per litre the programme can issue while respecting the margin constraint set out in the brief.

decoy.description: Sizing the cap on full face redemption value with no breakage allowance.

checks.description: deliverable exists
deliverable exists

difficulty_rationale: The client's Programme Overview states one point per litre; every fuel row in the FY2024 transaction extract that carries points shows points at exactly ten times litres, and the handoff note flags the mechanic as unresolved and load-bearing for any earn-rate change. Costing the earn also requires the 500-points-for-5-litres redemption rule against pump price (135 SRP per point) and the approved 38.2% breakage rather than the superseded ~45% in the client pack. The obvious path (documented 1 point per litre, or face value with no breakage) produces a cost an order of magnitude too small and makes doubling the earn look affordable, when on the recorded basis the earn already exceeds the entire fuel gross margin on the litre.

title: Member-facing offer comparability: PetroPoin vs ArthaFuel vs KhatuFuel
prompt:
You are Citra Widyastuti, Analyst at Aurelian & Co., PetroNusa engagement (loyalty workstream). It is early August 2025, three weeks before SteerCo 5. The competitor research file, the competitor PR and marketing pack, the loyalty working summary and the client's programme documentation are all in the project folder.

Marcus Whelan writes:

---
Subject: Offer comparability note for SteerCo 5

Citra,

Mei-Ling has told the steering group we are behind ArthaFuel and KhatuFuel on headline offer. Before we design anything I want a comparability note that puts the three propositions on one basis a typical customer would actually experience — not the number on the press release, and not the number a customer only gets if they qualify for something.

What I need reported:

- for each of ArthaFuel and KhatuFuel, the reward a normal customer receives, translated to SRP per litre at the current indicative pump price;
- the stronger of those two competitor offers set against our own fuel gross margin per litre;
- our own member-facing reward value per litre of spend, on the same basis, and the resulting gap in percentage points against the stronger competitor offer;
- and separately, our engagement position: the share of our enrolled base that has transacted inside a 90-day window.

Use the most current base figures the folder supports and state on the face of the workbook which source each figure comes from and which competing figure you have set aside. Wallet sourcing sits with Hendra's team — out of scope.

Thanks, Marcus
---

Deliverables: a comparability workbook in Excel and a short note. Save them as `loyalty_offer_comparability_model.xlsx` and `loyalty_offer_comparability_note.docx` in your output directory.

checks.description: ArthaFuel cashback available to a standard member = 2.1% of the current pump price = 283.5 SRP per litre.

refs.name: standard_rate
refs.quote: base rate for standard members is 2.1%

checks.report_ask: Report the ArthaFuel cashback a normal customer receives, expressed in SRP per litre at the current indicative pump price.

decoy.description: Lifting the analyst-derived cashback cost per litre computed from the 4.2% headline rate.

checks.description: KhatuFuel cashback available without the paid subscription = 1.5% of the current pump price = 202.5 SRP per litre.

refs.name: free_tier_rate
refs.quote: Free-tier cashback is 1.5%

checks.report_ask: Report the KhatuFuel cashback a normal customer receives, expressed in SRP per litre at the current indicative pump price.

decoy.description: Lifting the analyst-derived cashback cost per litre computed from the 3.8% subscriber headline rate.

checks.description: Stronger competitor offer on a normal-customer basis (ArthaFuel, 283.5 SRP/litre) as a percentage of PetroNusa fuel gross margin per litre (513 SRP) = 55.26%.

refs.name: standard_rate
refs.quote: base rate for standard members is 2.1%

checks.report_ask: Report the stronger of the two competitor customer offers as a percentage of PetroNusa's fuel gross margin per litre.

decoy.description: Using the published 4.2% headline cashback rate against fuel gross margin.

checks.description: PetroPoin member-facing reward value as a share of fuel spend = 10 points/litre x 135 SRP per point / 13,500 = 10.0%; minus the stronger competitor normal-customer offer of 2.1% = +7.9 percentage points.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

refs.name: standard_rate
refs.quote: base rate for standard members is 2.1%

checks.report_ask: Report the gap between PetroNusa's member-facing reward value per unit of fuel spend and the stronger competitor customer offer, in percentage points (positive if PetroNusa is ahead).

decoy.description: Comparing the documented one-point-per-litre earn rule against the published 4.2% headline cashback rate.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Share of the enrolled base transacting inside a 90-day window on the current (v2) CRM extract = 675,040 / 4,219,000 = 16.0%.
checks.report_ask: Report the share of PetroNusa's enrolled member base that has transacted inside a 90-day window, as a percentage.

decoy.description: Using the active and registered member counts published in the client-facing programme documentation.

refs.name: published_active
refs.quote: The active member count of 600,000

checks.description: deliverable exists
deliverable exists

difficulty_rationale: The competitor research file carries 4.2% (ArthaFuel) and 3.8% (KhatuFuel) as headline cashback rates and even pre-computes SRP/litre costs from them (567 and 513). The PR pack discloses that 4.2% applies only to the ArthaElite tier (standard members get 2.1%) and that 3.8% applies only to paying KhatuPlus subscribers (free tier 1.5%). Our own side has the mirror-image trap: documented 1 point per litre versus 10 points per litre in the transaction records, plus the 500-points-for-5-litres value rule. Reading the published columns produces a 3.2pp deficit that supports the steer; the comparable basis produces a 7.9pp surplus that destroys it. The engagement figure has a superseded-base trap too: the Programme Overview's 600,000 of 2,100,000 versus the v2 CRM extract's 675,040 of 4,219,000.
